headline: HUMF's integrity check was watched, and it PASSED ON WRONG BYTES TWICE, for two unrelated reasons. crc32 can be REPAIRED in 0.035 ms by a linear solve, so a payload with a flipped weight byte and four adjusted padding bytes was accepted, marked CLEAN and counted TRUSTED. And the check compares the SOURCE to the DESTINATION, so a source that rotted in place was compared with a faithful copy of its own rot and passed -- after which the two copies AGREE and every later check confirms the corruption. Neither is a flaw in crc32. ERROR DETECTION IS NOT IDENTITY.

THE_FORGERY.method: 32x32 GF(2) solve over 4 chosen bytes, not a search

through_the_fabric.fault_control: CAUGHT: integrity check FAILED transferring W into MOCK_EXTERNAL_VRAM
through_the_fabric.verdict: THE FABRIC ACCEPTED WRONG BYTES AND MARKED THEM CLEAN AND TRUSTED

WHAT_CRC32_ACTUALLY_BUYS.reading: crc32 is EXCELLENT at the thing it was designed for. The forgery is not evidence that it is a bad error detector; it is evidence that error detection is not identity.
WHAT_CRC32_ACTUALLY_BUYS.why_this_half_matters: Reporting the forgery without this would be a smear. crc32 caught EVERY accidental corruption in 4000 trials of each class. It stays the per-transfer fault check; it stops being the thing that answers 'is this the same object'.

without_a_sealed_identity.verdict: THE ROT PROPAGATED THROUGH A CHECK THAT REPORTED SUCCESS. The per-transfer check compares SOURCE to DESTINATION, so a faithful copy of corrupt bytes is exactly what it is looking for. Worse: afterwards the two copies AGREE, so every later check confirms the corruption.

with_a_sealed_identity.message: refusing to transfer W out of APPLE_UM: the source no longer matches the identity sealed at registration (4d03115716aa4f5b vs 5adfa153ce0b5065). Nothi

TRUST_DECAY_NOW_HAS_A_MECHANISM.the_hole: a copy verified once was TRUSTED FOREVER and nothing ever re-asked. Trust was a fact with no age, so 'verified' silently meant 'was verified, at some moment, possibly a thousand events ago'.

what_was_built.Materialization.verified_at: the fabric event at which this copy's trust was last established
what_was_built.Humf.epoch: a monotonic EVENT counter, not a clock -- wall time is not what invalidates a copy, activity is, and a counter cannot drift
what_was_built.Humf.audit(identity): re-check every copy against the sealed identity NOW; a diverged copy goes UNKNOWN
what_was_built.Humf.stale_verifications(max_age): what you are relying on that has not been looked at recently
what_was_built.HumfObject.content_digest: blake2b-128 of the value, computed BY THE FABRIC at registration -- the only value here a transport cannot influence
what_was_built.mark_written UNSEALS: an identity check that fires on legitimate writes is an identity check somebody turns off

audit_finds_what_nothing_else_would_touc.why_it_matters: Nothing in the fabric had a reason to touch this copy. Without an audit its trust rested on a check from epoch 1 and would have rested there forever.

age.note: an event counter, not a clock -- wall time is not what invalidates a copy

a_write_unseals.audit_says: value is UNSEALED (written in APPLE_UM); there is nothing to check against until seal_value()
a_write_unseals.why: an identity check that fires on legitimate writes is an identity check somebody turns off

machine_real_rates_GB_s.paid_per: ONCE PER OBJECT at seal, plus once per transfer on the SOURCE only. The round-trip check on the destination stays crc32, because that check is against a FAULT and crc32 caught 100% of every fault class measured.

AND_IT_IS_NOT_FREE.ratio_on_this_machine: blake2b-128 1.387 GB/s against crc32 35.526 GB/s = 25.6x slower. Against a 5 GB/s bridge an unconditional re-hash costs ~3.6x the transfer it protects; against Apple UM at 589.73 GB/s it costs ~425x. THE CHECK IS MORE EXPENSIVE THAN THE MOVE.
AND_IT_IS_NOT_FREE.mock_caveat: the 14.73x is against a SIMULATED transfer whose bandwidth is a knob; it is reported because it is what the fabric actually did, and the bandwidth ratio above is the number that transfers to real hardware
AND_IT_IS_NOT_FREE.the_bimodal_arm_is_not_noise: only_if_unverified_for_8_events shows 1217% IQR BY CONSTRUCTION -- the first transfer pays the hash and the rest do not. Reported rather than smoothed.
AND_IT_IS_NOT_FREE.resolution: identity_recheck_age: 0 = every transfer (default, safe), k = only when the source has gone k events unverified, None = registration only. THIS IS THE DECAY MODEL PAYING FOR ITSELF: re-verify what has gone unlooked-at, not what was just checked. A production ADP on a high-bandwidth link should set k, and the receipt says so rather than leaving a default nobody can afford.

claim_boundary.the_round_trip_blind_spot_is_UNCHANGED: the destination check still validates copy_out, not what a KERNEL reads. compute_skew still passes it. Sealing the SOURCE does nothing about that and it is not claimed to.
claim_boundary.no_hostile_transport_is_modelled: substitute_next hands the fabric chosen bytes; it does not model an adversary who also sees the sealed digest. The realistic threat on a bridge is a buggy driver reusing a stale buffer, not an attacker
claim_boundary.blake2b_is_not_proven_here: it is used as a standard construction, not analysed
claim_boundary.mock_only: no real external device; the fabric's state machine is what is graded
claim_boundary.rot_is_injected_not_observed: no bit rot was witnessed on this machine
